messages:
marta: Heads-up — I'm opening a quick thread to align on the viewer->editor role split we're about to ship. Need to confirm audit log semantics and KMS key handling for legacy tokens.
liam: SGTM. what's the proposed mapping? are we doing granular scopes or just renaming?
denise: We're moving to scoped roles per project: viewer.project, editor.project, admin.org. Not just rename — some UI gating will change (hide billing, restrict API key creation).
arjun: Important: legacy tokens still contain the old role string. We need a shim so backend treats them as viewer.project:* or editor.project:* depending on org mapping. Also impacts KMS-wrapped secrets referencing role claims.
marta: Right. Proposal: add a compatibility layer in access-checker that translates legacy "viewer" -> "viewer.project:default" unless a project claim is present. We'll log an audit event with "legacy_mapping": true.
liam: Can we avoid double-encrypting in KMS when we rewrap tokens? ops concern.
arjun: We won't rewrap tokens automatically. We only re-encrypt when rotation occurs. But access-checker needs to fetch key metadata to assert which key ID signed/encrypted the blob. That metadata must be present in the audit log entry.
marta: Example audit payload we want: `{"actor":"<user>","action":"auth.token.use","role_claim":"viewer","mapped_role":"viewer.project:default","kms_key_id":"projects/prod/keys/rw-1"}`
denise: That looks good. Also add `role_mapping_version` so we can roll forward/backwards in logs.
liam: How do we surface this to UI? product wants to show an explicit warning when legacy tokens are used so customer can rotate.
marta: UI: small banner on API keys page when token has legacy role OR when access-checker emits legacy_mapping. Banner text: "This key uses legacy role semantics and may have expanded permissions — rotate to scoped keys." Link to docs.
security-oncall: Important security question: is there any condition where legacy->scoped mapping could elevate privileges?
arjun: Good catch. The shim must be conservative: if token had project claim empty and user's org has more than one project, map to the most-restrictive default (deny create API keys, deny billing.view). Essentially map to the intersection of viewer perms across projects.
marta: We'll add an integration test: create legacy token, simulate org with multiple projects, assert mapped_role does NOT include editor perms.
denise: I'll add the UI gating flags behind `rbac_ux_v2` remote flag and wire up the banner when the audit event exists.
liam: Rollout plan?
marta: Phase 1: server-side shim + audit-only logging (no UI changes), internal canary 10% orgs for 48h. Phase 2: enable UI banner + rotate prompts for 25% of orgs. Phase 3: enforce mapped roles (deny expanded perms) + full rollout.
security-oncall: Please create a runbook for incident where mapping behaves badly (e.g., incorrectly grants editor). Include rollback flag `rbac_backward_compat=false`.
arjun: I'll add the `rbac_backward_compat` feature flag and a metric `rbac.mapping.legacy_mapped` to telemetry. Also will emit a trace id in the audit entry for easy correlation.
marta: Can someone confirm KMS auditing requirements? We need to store key id in logs, but not key material. Also need a short TTL for log retention on these audit entries for PII minimization?
denise: Logs are fine to keep standard retention (90d) for audit. We must mask user IPs per privacy policy.
liam: (typo) liam: FYI, I opened a design doc with sample event schemas and UX screenshots: https://go/redux/rbac-legacy-migration (internal)
marta: Thanks. Action items: @arjun add feature flag + metric + trace id. @denise implement UI flag and banner. @liam update docs and customer comms. @security-oncall write runbook and approve retention. I'll own server shim and tests.
audit-bot: New audit rule suggested: alert when `legacy_mapping==true` and `mapped_role` contains any editor/admin perms.
security-oncall: Ack. We'll add that alert to pager rotation for the first 72h of Phase 3.
marta: Cool. If no one objects I'll start the PR today and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
